description: Mark reveals that Bjarne left a very drunk voicemail on Saturday night. A dismissive answer can delay the clue until a follow-up or Day 3.

openingMessages.speaker: Mark
openingMessages.text: Hey, one more thing. Did you ever listen to that voicemail you left me?

choices.text: Voicemail? I don't remember leaving one.
I probably called you about something work-related.
Whatever it was, it couldn't have been that important.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Oh. Well, it was pretty late Saturday night.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: You sounded... pretty out of it, to be honest. Like, really drunk. I could barely understand half of what you were saying.

choices.text: Did I say what I was apologizing for?
I don't remember any of that.
Well, that's embarrassing. Let's forget about it.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Hah, sure. You sounded like you were having a fantastic time, if by fantastic you mean barely capable of forming a sentence.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Don't worry, your secret's safe with me.

lines.speaker: Pragmatist
lines.text: A drunken voicemail. Wonderful. Our past self apparently had a very productive weekend.

choices.text: I don't remember much of it, honestly.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Maybe. But you don't usually call me that late unless something's going on.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Just saying.

lines.speaker: Detective
lines.text: A voicemail, Saturday night, and a missed call. This is worth following up.

choices.text: Actually, what did I sound like?
You're probably right. I'll listen to it later.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Pretty drunk, man. You kept apologizing about something. I couldn't make out what.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I bet you were celebrating, though maybe a bit too much.

choices.text: Did I say what I was apologizing for?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Not really. You kept repeating something about having messed things up.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I think you said something like 'I don't know how to fix it.' Then you started rambling about something else.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I wish I'd been able to pick up when you called.

lines.speaker: Grand Architect
lines.text: He sounds genuinely worried. We should take that seriously.

choices.text: I appreciate you worrying about me.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yeah, I figured. I didn't think much of it at first, but you didn't sound like your usual self.

choices.text: Maybe I was just celebrating too hard.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Hah. Trust me, I'm not holding it against you.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Although, if you're going to leave drunken voicemails, at least make them entertaining next time.

choices.text: I'll try to make the next one more coherent.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Maybe not. Still wish I could've been there.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Dude, no. You sounded like someone who was having a rough night. There's a difference.

choices.text: Thanks. I needed to hear that.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Don't make it weird, man. You're my best friend. It's part of the job.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Just make sure you hydrate before your next birthday celebration.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Alright. Just don't ignore it if you think something's wrong.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Anytime, man. I'm around if you need me.
